# DCT reference — read on demand

This client-neutral reference is installed at `paths.config_dir() / "dct-reference.md"`, resolved by the integration at call time. Read the resolved file named by this client's bounded instruction block when needed; do not paste the full reference into global instructions. A supported client integration installs workflows for that host; a generic MCP connection does not establish hooks, publishers or native tasks.

## Workflow inventory

- `clog` — [dct] Add a changelog entry to the dct database. Use when: "clog", "changelog", "log this change", or right after finishing any change ("just fixed/added X") — in any language. Entry: `add_changelog`. Explicit only: false.
- `commit` — [dct] Commit explicitly requested work after exact staged-files/message/changelog consent. Entry: `dct clog candidates`. Explicit only: false.
- `dct-import` — [dct] Explicit import of approved markdown tracking files, plan anchors and historical changelog rows. Entry: `ingest_plan_file / import_released_changelog`. Explicit only: true.
- `dct-init` — [dct] Explicit setup: diagnose/repair the current client integration and register this project. Entry: `dct doctor`. Explicit only: true.
- `handoff` — [dct] End-of-session workflow — flag next-sprint items and leave a handoff prompt. Use when: "handoff", "end session", "wrap up" — in any language. Entry: `handoff_work`. Explicit only: false.
- `pickup` — [dct] Start-of-session workflow — read last handoff, show current sprint, propose first action. Use when: "pickup", "resume", "where were we", "what’s next", "back to work" — in any language. Entry: `pickup_work`. Explicit only: false.
- `plan-resolve-uncertain` — [dct] Explicitly classify indexed uncertain plan sections with configured rules/command or manual choices. Entry: `set_plan_section_type / resolve_uncertain_sections`. Explicit only: true.
- `plan-status` — [dct] Cross-plan progress dashboard — per-plan done/total checkpoints, uncertain sections, last scan. Use when: "plan status", "plan progress", "how far along is the plan", "what’s left in the plans", or the user asks about overall progress of planned work — in any language. Entry: `list_plans / get_plan`. Explicit only: false.
- `release` — [dct] Release a version with ONE question — dct first checks everything the release will do (the commit of uncommitted changes, the entries, the changelog section, the version files, the push), the owner sees one screen and answers once, then the local `dct release` workflow commits, stamps, tags and pushes, each verified. Use when: "release", "bump version", "ship it" — in any language. Entry: `dct release plan`. Explicit only: false.
- `track` — [dct] Create a tracked item (issue / todo / feature / idea / improvement). Use when: "track this", "add issue/todo/feature", "bug", "idea", "refactor" — in any language. Type mapping lives in the create_item tool description. Entry: `create_item`. Explicit only: false.
- `track-list` — [dct] List and search tracked items across projects, priority-grouped, with file hotspots. Use when: "list issues", "what’s open", "backlog", "show todos" — in any language. Entry: `list_items`. Explicit only: false.
- `track-resolve` — [dct] Resolve or close a tracked item. Use when: "resolve issue", "close item", "done with #42", "wont fix" — in any language. Entry: `resolve_item`. Explicit only: false.
- `track-update` — [dct] Update a tracked item — status, priority, fields, sprint membership. Use when: "update item #N", "change priority", "start working on #N", "wip", "add/remove from sprint" — in any language. Entry: `update_item`. Explicit only: false.
- `triage` — [dct] Run a review's findings through the dct triage ledger: record consolidated findings, build and publish the triage page from the ledger, take an agent's prefill as proposals, and close with the owner's answers. Use when: "record the findings", "build/publish the triage page", "Codex filled in the proposals", "redeploy the triage", the owner pastes the page's decision text, or "accept the proposals as final" — in any language. Entry: `open_triage`. Explicit only: false.

Explicit-only workflows require the user's named request. The remaining descriptions select a use case; they never expand consent to commit, push, release, deploy, publication or instruction edits. Prefer the installed native workflow, using its complete self-contained contract.

## Tool and identity conventions

Discover only tools needed by the selected branch, using the current host's available discovery mechanism. Invoke tools with separate top-level parameters from their actual descriptions; illustrative `mcp__dct__` prefixes name DCT tools, not a requirement for one host's namespace. An unavailable operation is a readable capability refusal, never a reason for direct SQL or ad hoc Python writes.

Use the available MCP discovery mechanism. No client-specific discovery tool, task mirror, hooks or publisher is assumed.

Use truthful actor identity in `created_by` and `consumed_by`. Only the true client is mandatory. Model, session identifier and session link are included only when supplied by the host; never invent them.

A project suffix is included only from a prior successful DCT response or an explicit user-supplied slug, never a directory, worktree or task-title guess. UTC is included only from an actual provided clock, known host time context or a time tool; no approximate time. Otherwise omit unknown components entirely, including project and time: never fill them with `unknown`, `?`, `0000` or guessed values. Server-created `created_at` / `consumed_at` timestamps remain separate ledger facts.

Use `<known_actor_identity>` in calls. A client-only identity such as `Codex` or `Claude Code` is sufficient when nothing else is known. Full-format example, ONLY when all components are known: `<true client>[-<host-supplied model>] @ <verified project slug> <actual UTC time>`. The same known-component rule applies to creation and consumption.

No mandatory extra lookup or preflight is added to AUTO pickup. Preserve its one-call path; do not obtain a slug by a guessed directory mapping, call a writer to bypass a read-only schema refusal, or require a clock lookup merely to fill an optional component. A status question remains a pure read with no `consumed_by` required.

Identify the actual assistant client. Capability and identity information must come from the running host.

Creation/fetch returns integer primary keys; retain them as handles. Write acknowledgements can be minimal scalar dictionaries, not a full record. Fetch full context deliberately (`get_item`, `get_handoff`, `get_plan`). Plan MCP identifiers are integer primary keys; CLI plan/section aliases are explicit ULIDs guarded by project, never polymorphic ids.

Structured list views return `{cols, rows}`: map fields using the returned column names. `list_items` brief rows have no descriptions or source_file; use `view="full"` and `format="dict"` for full rows only when needed. `list_handoffs` gives 200-character prompt previews; `get_handoff` supplies the complete prompt/context summary. Empty project generally detects the server CWD, not an explicit cross-project request; the agent's actual checkout may differ, so pass the selected slug when relevant.

When a shared read (`get_context_snapshot` or `pickup_work(consume="false")`, CLI `dct pickup --consume never`) refuses with SchemaNotReady, explain that setup or a schema upgrade is required. Propose `dct db upgrade` with explicit consent, then retry the original read only after that migration succeeds. Never invoke an unrelated writer to trigger a hidden migration. A SQLite reader may create WAL/SHM sidecars; it does not initialize the database, change journal mode, schema or data. Do not infer this guarantee for other list/get tools.

## Workflow use without duplication

Each installed native skill contains its complete workflow and refusal/recovery contract. Invoke the skill for the selected workflow through the current host's supported discovery. No installed documentation path or client-specific slash syntax is required. Release effects require the local `dct release` executor; missing CLI is a readable refusal, never ledger-only emulation.

- **Language.** A quoted question, option, screen or report fixes what it
  says, not its wording: write it in the language of the conversation. Keep
  unchanged: identifiers, commands, paths, file contents, commit messages,
  changelog entries, short titles and anything shown verbatim.

The common consent boundary is the exact readable proposal before the user's explicit response. A selected default, timeout, silence, unattended run, old handoff or generated proposal is never approval. Changed scope requires a fresh concrete preview; reuse unchanged explicit consent already given. A report is not a consent request. Keep every proposal word visible before acceptance; hidden thinking, truncated content and a reference to an unavailable screen do not suffice.

Use the current host's eligible consent UI when it exposes complete previews; otherwise show the full decision material in visible text and ask for the explicit reply. Workflow references to dialog previews/Details pages mean the same complete readable content, translated to the current host's supported presentation. Never depend on hidden thinking, omitted pages or a Plan-only/optional-question-only permission tool.

## Type triggers — natural language → item_type

Map the phrase the user actually used to the closest type. No type cue in
the phrase → `todo` (the most neutral bucket), without a question. Ask about
the type only when the phrase is genuinely ambiguous — it carries cues for two
different types ("a bug, or maybe a new feature?") — and the choice changes
the scope of the work; otherwise pick the closer type and write.

| User says (EN / PL) | item_type | When to pick |
|---|---|---|
| "problem", "bug", "issue", "crash", "broken", "error", "doesn't work", "regression" / "problem", "błąd", "bug", "crash", "nie działa", "popsute", "zepsute" | **issue** | Observable defect in existing code/system. Reproducible wrong behavior. |
| "todo", "task", "action item", "need to", "must do" / "todo", "zadanie", "zrobić", "do zrobienia", "trzeba" | **todo** | Concrete work that's neither a bug nor a new user-visible capability. Generic "stuff to do". |
| "feature", "add X", "new capability", "let's build", "we should have" / "feature", "ficzer", "funkcja", "dodajmy", "zbudujmy", "nowa funkcja" | **feature** | New user-visible capability that doesn't exist yet. |
| "idea", "maybe", "what if", "consider", "brainstorm", "explore" / "pomysł", "idea", "a może", "rozważ", "zastanów się", "pomyślmy" | **idea** | Exploratory — not yet decided to build. May become a feature later. |
| "improvement", "refactor", "polish", "cleanup", "tidy up", "make X nicer" / "ulepszenie", "poprawa", "poprawmy", "polerka", "cleanup", "refactor", "uporządkuj" | **improvement** | Existing thing works but could be better (refactor, UX polish, perf, docs). |

### Examples

| Phrase | item_type | Why |
|---|---|---|
| "dodaj jako problem że parser się wywala na pustych plikach" | issue | "problem" + observable broken behavior |
| "dodaj ficzer, chcę zrobić dark mode" | feature | "ficzer" + new capability |
| "a może pomyślmy nad wtyczkami?" | idea | "a może" + exploratory |
| "trzeba uporządkować ten moduł parsera" | improvement | "uporządkować" + existing code |
| "dodaj todo — wysłać PR do review" | todo | explicit "todo", generic task |

## Status questions versus pickup commands

What the user said decides whether a handoff is consumed:

- **An instruction to continue** — on an unambiguous "continue" / "pickup" /
  "resume" (or `pickup` itself) the call consumes the single matching
  handoff (AUTO mode). All three commands have the same accepted consume behavior.
- **A status question** — "where were we", "what's next", "what's the state"
  → `pickup_work(project="", consume="false")`, a PURE READ, no `consumed_by`
  needed: report the state and say that a handoff is waiting and that
  "continue" picks it up. A request to only look ("show the handoff but keep
  it", an audit) is the same read.
- A word the user merely quotes or mentions ("what does "continue" do?") is
  not a command; only a request addressed to you counts.

## Gate and correction rules

The packaged `add_checkpoint` description defines required gates and explicit exceptions. Evaluate a gate by its recorded condition and required evidence, not a client-specific convention. A person's act or approval needs that person's confirmation; unchanged explicit confirmation is reused. A gate is rejected only on the user's decision (full gate policy: `add_checkpoint`), never independently to close an item. A stale or missing required check leaves it pending.

Cheap explicit tracking writes acknowledge their saved ids and a correction hint; an idea merely mentioned does not authorize a write or implementation. Complete checkpoints when proven, reject an obsolete task checkpoint on the scoped owner decision, and preserve ledger history.

## Checkpoints when work starts

No checkpoints at creation: the plan comes when work on the item starts —
`track-update` "start working on #N" (status → `in_progress`) proposes at
least 3 checkpoints when the work is a non-trivial feature or improvement, or
when the user asks to break the work down. Add them now only when the user
asks for that breakdown.

When the update starts work on an item (status → `in_progress`: "start
working on #N", "wip"), look at its checkpoints and its description in the
`get_item` result. An item that already has checkpoints keeps its plan: name
the next pending one and add nothing.

When work starts on a non-trivial feature or improvement — or when the user
asks to break the work down — propose a plan of at least 3 checkpoints:
concrete, actionable steps, as many as the work needs (3 is a minimum, never
a cap), written at once with `mcp__dct__add_checkpoint(item_id, text)`
(remember each id) and listed under the acknowledgement. The user adjusts it
in plain words: `mcp__dct__reject_checkpoint(id)` drops a step the user
removes (ledger-kept), `add_checkpoint` adds one.

A small bug or a one-line fix starts with no checkpoints: name the next step
in the acknowledgement instead of writing an artificial plan. A complex issue
or todo may get checkpoints when its work has several real steps, with no
fixed minimum taken from its type.

## Stored commit preferences

**Trailers** follow the project's stored preferences from the Step 1
`list_projects` row, applied without a question:

- `commit_co_authored_by` true → a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer (the actual host-supplied identity); false → none.
- `commit_session_link` true → the session link the client gives for this
  session (only its real host-supplied link); false → none. A session
  link is written only on a stored true (yes).
- null = not answered yet (never a "no"): ask ONCE — one decision interaction
  before the screen, both preferences in it — store the answers with
  `dct project trailers <slug> --co-authored-by on|off --session-link on|off`
  and apply them; the question never comes again for that project.
